conventions.money_inputs: Currency inputs are text fields with thousands separators (#totalSalaryInput, #deductionInput, #husbandSalaryInput, #wifeSalaryInput, #husbandDeductionInput, #wifeDeductionInput, #ptkpBase, #ptkpMarried, #ptkpSpouse, #ptkpDependent). Set them by typing the digits and dispatching input+change events, then blur.
conventions.split_slider: #splitPct is a range input 0..100 = the wife's share of the household salary in Total mode. Set its value and dispatch input+change.
conventions.modes: #modeBtnTotal = Total + Split % mode (uses #totalSalaryInput, #splitPct, #deductionInput). #modeBtnSplit = Husband + Wife mode (uses the four individual inputs).
conventions.ladder: The bracket ladder lives in #bracketsContainer as one .bracket-row per bracket, three inputs per row in DOM order: From (auto-filled), To, Rate (%). Rows are numbered 1..n from the top. The last row's To is the open bound. Refer to 'row k To' / 'row k Rate' below. The ladder is on the 'PTKP & Brackets' tab (.ctrl-tab[data-tab=advanced]).
conventions.reading_money: Read a money figure by stripping everything except digits, '-' and '.', then Number(). Record numbers as JS numbers, not strings. Record the raw text separately where a *_text key is asked for.
conventions.ladder_string: Where a 'ladder_*' key is asked for, encode the ladder on screen as rows joined by '|', each row 'FROM-TO@RATE' using plain integers with no separators, RATE as printed (e.g. 5 or 5.5), and the open bound written as inf. Example of the format only: '0-1000@1|1000-inf@2'.
conventions.reset: Every case starts from a fresh page load followed by a click on #resetBtn, then the ladder is checked/edited as the case says. Unless a case says otherwise: #dependents=0, Total mode, #deductionInput=0.
conventions.statutory_ladder_setup: Where a case says 'ladder = statutory', make the ladder on screen read exactly: row1 0-60000000@5, row2 60000000-250000000@15, row3 250000000-500000000@25, row4 500000000-5000000000@30, row5 5000000000-inf@35, editing rows if the shipped defaults differ. Record whether any edit was needed in the runner notes.

cases.title: Crossover search: an exact tie at a round salary, and a ladder with two crossings

steps: Part A: Reset, ladder = statutory, #dependents=0, Total mode, #totalSalaryInput=500,000,000, #splitPct=30, #deductionInput=0. Read the Crossover Analysis card #crossoverInfo.

Part B: keep the inputs of Part A, then edit the ladder: set row 3 To = 10,000,000,000 (this should remove the brackets beneath it per the page's own tooltip), then set row 3 Rate = 5 and the last row's Rate = 5. Confirm the ladder on screen and record it. Read #crossoverInfo again and read the Comparison detail table / chart 2 (Gabung − Pisah) across its whole salary range.

A 'crossover salary' is any household salary at which the card says the cheaper option changes. Parse every Rp figure the card presents as such; if the card says there is no crossover, record null and count 0.

cases.title: Bracket editor: collapse to one band, reversed bound, blank mid bound, non-monotonic rates, negative rate, last band forced open

steps: Common: Reset, ladder = statutory, #dependents=0, Total mode, #totalSalaryInput=500,000,000, #splitPct=50, #deductionInput=0. Re-run 'Reset + ladder = statutory' before every sub-state below.
State collapse: set row 1 To = 10,000,000,000.
State reversed: set row 2 To = 30,000,000 (below its own From).
State blank: clear row 2 To to an empty string and blur.
State dip: set row 3 Rate = 5 (rates now 5,15,5,30,35).
State negative: set row 1 Rate = -5.
State open: attempt to type 6,000,000,000 into the last row's To; record whether the input is disabled/readonly and what it shows afterwards.
